title: Feed the worms with kitchen waste
about: A worm box is a slow converter. In: kitchen scraps, paper bedding, air and moisture. Out: worm castings (a stable compost roots can feed on), a nutrient-carrying liquid, more worms, and a little heat. Here you fill the hopper, the gantry carries portions to the box, and the liquid drains into the tank under the bed and reaches the roots from below.

steps.title: You: put the scraps in the hopper
steps.why: The gantry cannot fetch waste from the kitchen. A person fills the hopper at the bed's near end: here, 1 kg of raw fruit and vegetable scraps. No meat, dairy or cooked food.

steps.title: Robot: carry a portion to the worm box
steps.why: The gantry lifts its tool, moves to the hopper, scoops a portion, travels the length of the bed and drops it at one spot of the worm box. How much is the feeder's advice: a small portion while it is still learning what these worms eat. Watch the overview camera.

steps.title: What changed in the worm box
steps.why: Fresh food makes the box wetter and heavier; the box's own sensors show it (see the Worm box panel). The box also follows the air's temperature, slowly. As the worms eat, about a third of the food drains down into the tank pipes as liquid.

steps.title: Robot: the next portion goes to the next spot
steps.why: Portions are spread in rotation across the box, so no corner is overloaded and the worms always have a quiet place. The proposal now names the next spot.
